name: Sotos Syndrome

criteria.description: Macrocephaly defined as head circumference >2 standard deviations above mean
Distinctive facial gestalt including frontal bossing, high anterior hairline, down-slanting palpebral fissures, and pointed chin
Global developmental delay or intellectual disability
Height and/or weight >2 standard deviations above mean for age
Pathogenic variant in NSD1 gene identified by molecular genetic testing

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of macrocephaly, characteristic facial features, and developmental delay; molecular confirmation supports diagnosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular testing for NSD1 mutations is confirmatory but not always necessary if clinical criteria are met

pathognomonic.notes: Head circumference significantly above age norms
Includes frontal bossing, high anterior hairline, down-slanting palpebral fissures
Delayed milestones in motor and cognitive domains
searchTerms: global delay in growth and skills

common.symptomName: Overgrowth (height and weight >2 SD above mean)
common.notes: Rapid growth in infancy and early childhood
Reduced muscle tone often present in infancy

occasional.notes: Including atrial septal defects and patent ductus arteriosus

rare.notes: Enlarged liver reported in isolated cases
Increased risk of certain tumors such as neuroblastoma

laboratory: Occasional mild elevation of liver enzymes
imaging: Brain MRI may show ventriculomegaly or delayed myelination
Skeletal X-rays reveal advanced bone age and scoliosis
genetic: Pathogenic variants in NSD1 gene detected by sequencing or deletion/duplication analysis
other: Growth charts showing accelerated growth velocity

distinguishingFeatures: Facial features differ with broad forehead and large ears
EZH2 gene mutations instead of NSD1

redFlags: Rapid head growth with neurological deterioration
Signs of tumor development (e.g., abdominal mass)
references: Tatton-Brown K, Rahman N. Sotos syndrome. Eur J Hum Genet. 2007;15(3):264-271.

Douglas J, Hanks S, Temple IK, et al. NSD1 mutations are the major cause of Sotos syndrome and occur in some cases of Weaver syndrome but are rare in other overgrowth phenotypes. Am J Hum Genet. 2003;72(1):132-143.
Kurotaki N, Harada N, Yoshiura K, et al. Haploinsufficiency of NSD1 causes Sotos syndrome. Nat Genet. 2002;30(4):365-366.
